vizqueryearth.title: Known issues in popular Earth-system datasets
vizqueryearth.description: Known issues that each dataset's producers document, gathered by Claude: every rule quotes its source page, and the quote was checked to be on that page, but no person has reviewed the periods and regions. Draw your area, give your dates and type your dataset (such as era5, glorys12 or woa23) to see which issues apply.

properties.name: ERA5/ERA5001
properties.title: ERA5 is too cold in the lower stratosphere, 2000-2006
properties.message: From 2000 to 2006 ERA5 fits radiosonde temperatures poorly in the stratosphere, with a cold bias in the lower stratosphere, and a warm bias higher up persists for much of the ERA5 period. ERA5.1, a re-run of ERA5 for 2000 to 2006 only, rectifies the lower stratospheric cold bias and better represents upper stratospheric temperature and stratospheric humidity.
properties.instruction: For 2000-2006, use ERA5.1 wherever the stratosphere matters. ERA5.1 comes from MARS (CDS API dataset 'reanalysis-era5.1-complete'), not from the CDS disks.

references.title: ERA5: data documentation, Known issues (Copernicus Knowledge Base, ECMWF)

evidence.quote: From 2000 to 2006, ERA5 has a poor fit to radiosonde temperatures in the stratosphere, with a cold bias in the lower stratosphere. In addition, a warm bias higher up persists for much of the ERA5 period.

properties.gathered_by: Claude, from the source page, whose quote was checked to be on it; the period and region were not reviewed by a person

properties.name: ERA5/ERA5002
properties.title: ERA5 is less reliable before 1946, with a cold stratosphere
properties.message: Before the mid-1940s ERA5 had no upper-air observations. On the yearly scale, global mean temperature for the early 1940s agrees less well with reconstructions based only on observations, and the lack of upper-air observations exposes a model cold bias in the lower stratosphere. Agreement is much better from the mid- to late-1940s onwards.
properties.instruction: Treat yearly global mean temperature and lower stratospheric temperature from the early 1940s with caution.

references.title: ERA5 reanalysis now available from 1940 (ECMWF Newsletter 175, Spring 2023)

evidence.quote: On the yearly scale, there is less agreement in global mean temperature for the early 1940s, while the lack of upper-air observations in these years also exposes a model cold bias in the lower stratosphere. Agreement is much better from the mid- to late-1940s onwards.

properties.gathered_by: Claude, from the source page, whose quote was checked to be on it; the period and region were not reviewed by a person

properties.name: ERA5/ERA5003
properties.title: Southern Hemisphere is sparsely observed before 1970
properties.message: ERA5 used no satellite data before 1970, and the in-situ observing system over the Southern Hemisphere was sparse; before the mid-1940s there were no upper-air observations at all. ECMWF says ERA5 should give a good estimate of the synoptic situation for large regions of the Northern Hemisphere from 1940. Where ERA5 is controlled more by the model than by observations, it should still describe low-frequency variability well.
properties.instruction: Use the ERA5 ensemble spread to judge when and where the fields are dominated by observations and where they are more controlled by the model.

references.title: ERA5 reanalysis now available from 1940 (ECMWF Newsletter 175, Spring 2023)

evidence.quote: In ERA5, no satellite data were used before 1970. The in‑situ observing system was sparse over the southern hemisphere, and before the mid‑1940s no upper‑air observations were available.

properties.gathered_by: Claude, from the source page, whose quote was checked to be on it; the period and region were not reviewed by a person

properties.name: ERA5/ERA5004
properties.title: Great Lakes 2 m temperature cycle too strong before 2014
properties.message: Before 2014 ERA5 did not use sea surface temperature over the Great Lakes to nudge its lake model. As a result, 2 metre temperature there has an annual cycle that is too strong, too cold in winter and too warm in summer.
properties.instruction: Treat the ERA5 2 metre temperature seasonal cycle over the Great Lakes before 2014 with caution, including trends that cross 2014.

references.title: ERA5: data documentation, Known issues (Copernicus Knowledge Base, ECMWF)

evidence.quote: Prior to 2014, the SST was not used over the Great Lakes to nudge the lake model. Consequently, the 2 metre temperature has an annual cycle that is too strong, with temperatures being too cold in winter and too warm in summer.

properties.gathered_by: Claude, from the source page, whose quote was checked to be on it; the period and region were not reviewed by a person

properties.name: ERA5/ERA5005
properties.title: Too little sea ice north of Greenland, 1979-1989
properties.message: From 1979 to 1989, in a region just to the north of Greenland, ERA5 sea-ice cover outside the melt season is too low, and hence 2 metre temperature is too high.
properties.instruction: Do not rely on ERA5 2 metre temperature trends north of Greenland that span the 1980s.

references.title: ERA5: data documentation, Known issues (Copernicus Knowledge Base, ECMWF)

evidence.quote: ERA5 sea-ice cover and 2 metre temperature: in the period 1979-1989, in a region just to the north of Greenland, the sea-ice cover outside of the melt season is too low and hence the 2 metre temperature is too high.

properties.gathered_by: Claude, from the source page, whose quote was checked to be on it; the period and region were not reviewed by a person

properties.name: ERA5/ERA5006
properties.title: Spurious snow in Iberia, December 1977 to March 1979
properties.message: Because erroneous in situ snow observations were assimilated, ERA5 has snow in Iberia throughout 1978, and 2 m temperature shows negative anomalies of several degrees Celsius. In the monthly means the erroneous snow depth lasts from December 1977 to March 1979. ERA5-Land has no snow there but inherits the 2 m temperature anomaly from its ERA5 forcing.
properties.instruction: Treat ERA5 snow depth and 2 m temperature, and ERA5-Land 2 m temperature, over Iberia from December 1977 to March 1979 as erroneous.

references.title: ERA5: data documentation, Known issues (Copernicus Knowledge Base, ECMWF)

evidence.quote: Snow present in Iberia throughout 1978 due to assimilation of erroneous in situ snow data. This has an effect on 2m temperature, which shows negative anomalies of several degrees Celsius.

properties.gathered_by: Claude, from the source page, whose quote was checked to be on it; the period and region were not reviewed by a person

properties.name: ERA5/ERA5007
properties.title: False cyclone over the Amundsen Sea, May to October 1996
properties.message: From May to October 1996 ERA5 has a highly unrealistic semi-permanent cyclone over the Amundsen Sea, which corrupts near-surface winds over the Southern Ocean near Antarctica. It comes from the wrong station altitude sometimes being reported for the nearest observation station.
properties.instruction: Treat ERA5 near-surface winds over the Amundsen Sea from May to October 1996 as unreliable.

references.title: ERA5: data documentation, Known issues (Copernicus Knowledge Base, ECMWF)

evidence.quote: From May-October 1996 there is a semi-permanent cyclone which appears in ERA5 over the Amundsen Sea region (approximately 74 to 68°S, 206-260°E) which is highly unrealistic. This is due to the wrong station altitude sometimes being reported for the nearest observation station.

properties.gathered_by: Claude, from the source page, whose quote was checked to be on it; the period and region were not reviewed by a person

properties.name: ERA5/ERA5008
properties.title: Spurious 10 m wind spikes at a few locations, 1979-2020
properties.message: A few times per year, ERA5's analysed low-level winds, such as the 10 m winds, become unrealistically large at one of a few apparently preferred locations, reaching about 300 m/s. The cause is an instability in the analysis method towards the end of the assimilation windows, and 100 m winds are sometimes affected too. From 19 February 2020, ERA5 replaces the analysed 10 m winds with the '4v' winds whenever either component exceeds 50 m/s.
properties.instruction: For dates from 1979 to 18 February 2020, check the source's tables of events where a 10 m wind component exceeds 50 m/s. For those times, use the '4v' 10 m wind components from 'reanalysis-era5-complete' (MARS), as the page's CDS API script shows.

references.title: ERA5: large 10m winds (Copernicus Knowledge Base, ECMWF)

evidence.quote: A few times per year, the analysed low-level winds, e.g. the 10m winds, become unrealistically large in a particular location, which varies amongst a few apparently preferred locations. The largest values seen so far are about 300 ms-1.

properties.gathered_by: Claude, from the source page, whose quote was checked to be on it; the period and region were not reviewed by a person

properties.name: GLORYS12/GLORYS12001
properties.title: Sea ice too thick in the Beaufort Gyre
properties.message: GLORYS12 piles up sea ice in the Beaufort Gyre, where it is almost 1 m thicker than Cryosat-2 in January 2014. The build-up stops the ice from melting well, so summer ice there is generally too thick. In the Central and Eurasian basins the ice is thinner than observed.

references.title: Lellouche et al. (2021), The Copernicus Global 1/12° Oceanic and Sea Ice GLORYS12 Reanalysis, Frontiers in Earth Science 9:698876

evidence.quote: The unrealistic piling up of sea ice thickness in the Beaufort Gyre present in all GLORYS reanalysis (Chevallier et al., 2017; Uotila et al., 2019) is also present in GLORYS12. Comparisons with Cryosat-2 in January 2014 (Figure 5A) show an overestimation of the order of almost 1 m in the area.

properties.gathered_by: Claude, from the source page, whose quote was checked to be on it; the period and region were not reviewed by a person

properties.name: GLORYS12/GLORYS12002
properties.title: South Equatorial Current too strong in tropical Pacific
properties.message: Compared with drogued drifters at 15 m, the main weakness in the surface currents is a tropical Pacific South Equatorial Current that is too strong. This is mainly due to a bias in the reference height (mean dynamic topography) used for assimilating altimetry.

references.title: Lellouche et al. (2021), The Copernicus Global 1/12° Oceanic and Sea Ice GLORYS12 Reanalysis, Frontiers in Earth Science 9:698876

evidence.quote: The main shortcoming concerns the tropical Pacific South Equatorial Current which is too strong in GLORYS12. It has been shown that this was mainly due to a bias in the reference height for the altimetry (Hamon et al., 2019).

properties.gathered_by: Claude, from the source page, whose quote was checked to be on it; the period and region were not reviewed by a person

properties.name: GLORYS12/GLORYS12003
properties.title: Temperature and salinity less reliable before 2004
properties.message: Before the Argo array arrived in 2004, far fewer in situ profiles constrain the reanalysis. Departures from in situ observations are about 0.75°C and 0.2 psu over 1993-2002, against 0.45°C and 0.1 psu in the Argo period. The paper says the arrival of Argo halved these departures.
properties.instruction: Treat temperature and especially salinity before 2004, and any trend computed across 2004, with caution.

references.title: Lellouche et al. (2021), The Copernicus Global 1/12° Oceanic and Sea Ice GLORYS12 Reanalysis, Frontiers in Earth Science 9:698876

evidence.quote: For instance, the representation of temperature and salinity is strongly impacted by the arrival of the global Argo array in 2004 reducing the departures from in situ observations by a factor of 2.

properties.gathered_by: Claude, from the source page, whose quote was checked to be on it; the period and region were not reviewed by a person

properties.name: GLORYS12/GLORYS12004
properties.title: Spurious jumps in eddy energy in 2002 and 2004
properties.message: Eddy kinetic energy has two artificial discontinuities. The first is a rise from early 2002 to 2007, caused by a change in the SST resolution used by the ERA-Interim forcing. The second is a rapid jump in 2004, when the 3D-VAR bias-correction window was shortened as Argo profiles arrived.
properties.instruction: Do not interpret changes in eddy energy, or in its seasonal amplitude, across 2002 or 2004 as real ocean changes.

references.title: Lellouche et al. (2021), The Copernicus Global 1/12° Oceanic and Sea Ice GLORYS12 Reanalysis, Frontiers in Earth Science 9:698876

evidence.quote: The time evolution of the monthly EKE clearly highlights two major discontinuities, which result from changes in the ERAinterim atmospheric forcing in 2002 and in the in situ observing system in 2004.

properties.gathered_by: Claude, from the source page, whose quote was checked to be on it; the period and region were not reviewed by a person

properties.name: GLORYS12/GLORYS12005
properties.title: Sea level drifts low against altimetry from 2004
properties.message: From 2004 the reanalysis sea level drifts low against the assimilated altimetry by about 0.25 mm per year. The gap reaches 1 cm by the end of 2016, with peaks of 2 cm, and is mainly linked to the orbit standard of the altimeter data. Global mean sea level rise is slightly below altimetry, and too much of it is thermal expansion, so the steric and mass parts are not split correctly.
properties.instruction: Do not use GLORYS12 to separate steric and mass (barystatic) contributions to sea level rise.

references.title: Lellouche et al. (2021), The Copernicus Global 1/12° Oceanic and Sea Ice GLORYS12 Reanalysis, Frontiers in Earth Science 9:698876

evidence.quote: However, from 2004, a bias is diagnosed, which tends to increase and reaches 1 cm at the end of the period, with peaks varying from 1 cm or even 2 cm at times. This means that GLORYS12 tends to become too low in comparison with altimetry by about 0.25 mm per year.

properties.gathered_by: Claude, from the source page, whose quote was checked to be on it; the period and region were not reviewed by a person

properties.name: JRA55DO/JRA55DO001
properties.title: Anti-cyclonic tropical cyclones, North Atlantic 1967-1987
properties.message: Many North Atlantic tropical cyclones between 1967 and 1987 rotate the wrong way (anti-cyclonically) in the JRA-55 analysis, so JRA55-do up to v1.4 has them too. Around each erroneous analysis the atmospheric fields are unrealistic within about 1000 km for the next 6 hours, and the footprint can last a few days.
properties.instruction: Use JRA55-do v1.5 or later (the final version is v1.6.0). These versions replace the surface fields around these cyclones with fields from 20CRv3.

references.title: User manual of JRA-55 based surface dataset for driving ocean–sea-ice models (JRA55-do), v1.6 (14 December 2024), Appendix C.11.1

evidence.quote: Erroneous behaviors are found for some tropical cyclones in the period from 1959 to 1987 in the original JRA-55 analysis. Specifically, lots of tropical cyclones have anti-cyclonic rotation in the JRA-55 analysis and the JRA55-do dataset.

properties.gathered_by: Claude, from the source page, whose quote was checked to be on it; the period and region were not reviewed by a person

properties.name: JRA55DO/JRA55DO002
properties.title: High-latitude air temperature tied to CORE, 1958-1978
properties.message: Before satellites, the sea ice under JRA-55 is largely climatological in the Southern Hemisphere and probably too extensive in the Labrador Sea. As a result, JRA-55 air temperature and humidity are unreliable there and suspiciously low near the ice edge, which can make deep water formation unrealistically strong in ocean models. To compensate, JRA55-do adds the smoothed monthly CORE-minus-JRA-55 difference to these fields poleward of 40°N and 50°S for 1958-1978.

references.title: JRA-55 based surface dataset for driving ocean–sea-ice models (JRA55-do), Tsujino et al., Ocean Modelling 130 (2018) 79–139, Section 3.3.4

evidence.quote: As a result, the air temperature and specific humidity of JRA-55 tend to be suspiciously low in the marginal sea-ice zones, specifically in the Labrador Sea, in the pre-satellite period, which can result in unrealistically strong deep water formation in ocean models. Thus, at latitudes poleward of 40°N or 50°S, we added the time series of the difference of the temperature and specific humidity between the adjusted JRA-55 and CORE (CORE minus the adjusted JRA-55) to the adjusted JRA-55 fields for 1958–1978.

properties.gathered_by: Claude, from the source page, whose quote was checked to be on it; the period and region were not reviewed by a person

properties.name: JRA55DO/JRA55DO003
properties.title: Pinatubo eruption missing from shortwave, 1991-1992
properties.message: The drop in downward shortwave radiation after the 1991 Mt. Pinatubo eruption is in CORE but missing from JRA-55 and JRA55-do. Models forced with JRA55-do cool around 1991 only because of low air temperatures assimilated into JRA-55. The producers found this insufficient to reproduce the observed cooling in 1991.

references.title: Evaluation of global ocean–sea-ice model simulations based on the experimental protocols of the Ocean Model Intercomparison Project phase 2 (OMIP-2), Tsujino et al., Geosci. Model Dev. 13, 3643–3708, 2020

evidence.quote: This eruption is absent in the OMIP-2 (JRA55-do) dataset, resulting in stronger cooling by 5 W m−2 only in OMIP-1 for the year 1991 according to Tsujino et al. (2018) (see their Fig. 22). The decline found in OMIP-2 is due to the low air temperature assimilated in the original JRA-55 analysis product, which turned out to be insufficient to reproduce the observed cooling in 1991.

properties.gathered_by: Claude, from the source page, whose quote was checked to be on it; the period and region were not reviewed by a person

properties.name: JRA55DO/JRA55DO004
properties.title: Southern Hemisphere westerly wind stress too strong
properties.message: Since v1.3, wind speed is adjusted with an offset rather than a multiplicative factor, which strengthens the zonal wind stress in the mid-latitude westerlies. Compared with the SCOW scatterometer climatology, the stress in the Northern Hemisphere mid-latitudes is close, but in the Southern Hemisphere it is too strong. It is still an improvement on raw JRA-55.

references.title: User manual of JRA-55 based surface dataset for driving ocean–sea-ice models (JRA55-do), v1.6 (14 December 2024), Appendix C.9

evidence.quote: The zonal wind stresses in the mid latitudes of the Northern Hemisphere get close to whereas those of the Southern Hemisphere get too strong relative to the Scatterometer Oceanic Wind Stress (SCOW) product (Risien and Chelton, 2008) in version 1.3.

properties.gathered_by: Claude, from the source page, whose quote was checked to be on it; the period and region were not reviewed by a person

properties.name: JRA55DO/JRA55DO005
properties.title: ITCZ wind adjustment weakens North Equatorial Countercurrent
properties.message: The adjustment corrects weak ITCZ winds in the raw reanalysis by increasing wind speed there. This wrongly strengthens the weaker mean easterlies along the ITCZ relative to their surroundings and weakens the wind stress curl north and south of it. Models forced with JRA55-do, as with CORE, simulate a too-weak eastward North Equatorial Countercurrent at 6-8°N and a sea surface height bias.

references.title: Evaluation of global ocean–sea-ice model simulations based on the experimental protocols of the Ocean Model Intercomparison Project phase 2 (OMIP-2), Tsujino et al., Geosci. Model Dev. 13, 3643–3708, 2020

evidence.quote: The weak wind variabilities in the Intertropical Convergence Zone (ITCZ) in the original reanalysis products have been adjusted by increasing the wind speed in both forcing datasets (see Fig. 10 of Tsujino et al., 2018). This wind speed increase results in the erroneous strengthening of the weaker mean easterly wind along the ITCZ relative to its surroundings, which was reproduced rather realistically in the original JRA-55 reanalysis.

properties.gathered_by: Claude, from the source page, whose quote was checked to be on it; the period and region were not reviewed by a person

properties.name: JRA55DO/JRA55DO006
properties.title: Uncertain wind direction off Central America
properties.message: JRA55-do rotates JRA-55 wind directions toward QuikSCAT using a fit that works in most regions but not in several coastal ones, where the rotation is tapered. The eastern tropical North Pacific off Central America is one of them, because orography strongly affects wind direction there. The producers say simulation results in these regions should be interpreted with some care.
properties.instruction: Interpret simulation results here with care. The rotation scripts are freely available and could be modified, for example to remove the rotation correction in such regions.

references.title: JRA-55 based surface dataset for driving ocean–sea-ice models (JRA55-do), Tsujino et al., Ocean Modelling 130 (2018) 79–139, Section 3.4.2

evidence.quote: The eastern tropical North Pacific off the coast of Central America is one of those regions where the wind direction is strongly affected by orography. Simulation results should be interpreted with some care in those regions.

properties.gathered_by: Claude, from the source page, whose quote was checked to be on it; the period and region were not reviewed by a person

properties.name: JRA55DO/JRA55DO007
properties.title: Greenland and Arctic runoff is climatology after 2016
properties.message: From v1.4, runoff from Greenland and from Canadian Arctic glaciers follows the monthly 1958-2016 series of Bamber et al. (2018). After 2016 it repeats the 2012-2016 monthly climatology, so it has no interannual variability.

references.title: User manual of JRA-55 based surface dataset for driving ocean–sea-ice models (JRA55-do), v1.6 (14 December 2024), Section 2.1 and Appendix C.10

evidence.quote: For the period before 1958 and after 2016, the monthly climatology from 1958 to 1962 and from 2012 to 2016 is used, respectively.

properties.gathered_by: Claude, from the source page, whose quote was checked to be on it; the period and region were not reviewed by a person

properties.name: JRA55DO/JRA55DO008
properties.title: River discharge too high in 1958
properties.message: River discharge in JRA55-do is excessive in 1958. JRA-55's land-surface model produced high runoff that year, and the adjustment could not correct it because it applies the 1963 factor to 1958-1962.

references.title: JRA-55 based surface dataset for driving ocean–sea-ice models (JRA55-do), Tsujino et al., Ocean Modelling 130 (2018) 79–139, Section 4

evidence.quote: The excessive river discharge in 1958 of JRA55-do occurred because the high runoff from the land-surface component of JRA-55 of that year could not be appropriately corrected by the present adjustment method that uses the multiplicative factor for 1963 during the period 1958–1962.

properties.gathered_by: Claude, from the source page, whose quote was checked to be on it; the period and region were not reviewed by a person

properties.title: GEBCO_2024 has gridding artifacts in the Arctic north of 70N

properties.title: GEBCO_2026 depths are offset in the North Pacific, 10N-64N
properties.message: Depth values in the GEBCO_2026 Grid are offset from those in GEBCO_2025 in the North Pacific between 10N and 64N; the errata page files it under the area off the north-west coast of the USA. properties.name: GEBCO/GEBCO007
properties.title: Depths between surveys are interpolated; see the TID grid
properties.message: The level of detail in the GEBCO grid depends on its source data: areas based on soundings with interpolation guided by satellite-derived gravity data show less detail than areas based on multibeam data. Where the grid comes from a pre-generated grid (TID 70), measured and interpolated areas cannot be told apart, so the whole region may appear mapped.
properties.instruction: Check the TID grid to see whether the cells in your area are based on measured data or on interpolation.

references.title: GEBCO TID Grid | GEBCO

evidence.quote: This difference in data source is reflected in the level of detail shown in the bathymetric grid.

properties.title: Main grid shows ice surface over Antarctica and Greenland
properties.message: The primary GEBCO grid contains land and ice-surface elevation. Under-ice topography and bathymetry for Greenland and Antarctica is in a separate version of the grid. Both are taken from BedMachine Greenland and BedMachine Antarctica.
properties.instruction: Use the under-ice topography version of the grid where you need the bed or seabed beneath the Greenland and Antarctic ice.

references.title: The GEBCO_2026 Grid | GEBCO

evidence.quote: The primary GEBCO_2026 grid contains land and ice surface elevation information. A version is also made available with under-ice topography/bathymetry information for Greenland and Antarctica.

properties.name: EN4/EN4001
properties.title: Analyses relax to climatology where data are sparse
properties.message: EN4 analysis values are partly set by observations and partly by background fields, as shown by the observation weight variables. In the long-term absence of observations, EN.4.2.2 analyses relax back to the 1971-2000 climatology, and the producers do not encourage using the analyses for trend analysis where observation weights are low.
properties.instruction: Check the observation weight variables before using the analysis fields, especially for long-term trends. Values near one mean observations shaped the analysis, and values near zero mean it is mostly background.

references.title: EN4: Frequently Asked Questions (Met Office Hadley Centre)

evidence.quote: We would not encourage the use of EN4 analyses for trend analysis in areas where the observation weights are low. In the long term absence of observations, EN.4.2.2 analyses will relax back to the 1971 - 2000 climatology.

properties.gathered_by: Claude, from the source page, whose quote was checked to be on it; the period and region were not reviewed by a person

properties.name: EN4/EN4002
properties.title: XBT and MBT bias corrections differ between members
properties.message: EN.4.2.2 provides four ensemble members (l09, g10, c13, c14). Each uses a different combination of mechanical (MBT) and expendable (XBT) bathythermograph bias corrections, and the guide shows that the choice changes results such as 0-700 m ocean heat content. Only XBT and MBT data are corrected.
properties.instruction: Repeat your analysis with all four ensemble members to see how much the bathythermograph corrections affect your conclusions.

references.title: EN.4.2.2 Product User Guide v1.0

evidence.quote: We encourage users to explore the impact of different ensemble members on their application to ensure that uncertainty arising from necessary, but imperfect, bathythermograph bias corrections is represented.

properties.gathered_by: Claude, from the source page, whose quote was checked to be on it; the period and region were not reviewed by a person

properties.name: EN4/EN4003
properties.title: Salinity much sparser than temperature before Argo
properties.message: MBTs (from the late 1930s) and XBTs (from the late 1960s) do not measure salinity, so after they appear far fewer profiles are good for salinity than for temperature. Coverage of the two becomes more similar once Argo is introduced, although an offset remains.

properties.name: WOA23/WOA23001
properties.title: Artificially high winter salinity in the Arctic
properties.message: The Arctic Ocean is sampled mostly in boreal summer, so the all-data first-guess salinity field is very fresh near the surface, while the few winter observations are much saltier. The objective analysis therefore gives artificially high winter salinities in some parts of the Arctic. The density stabilization step can then wrongly change winter salinity and create discontinuities in the stabilized temperature and salinity fields.
properties.instruction: Before relying on Arctic winter salinity, inspect the data distribution, statistical fields and objectively analyzed fields that the atlas provides.

references.title: World Ocean Atlas 2023, Volume 2: Salinity (NOAA Atlas NESDIS 90), Appendix C: Geographic salinity limitations

evidence.quote: Using such biased first-guess fields in the objective analysis procedure results in artificially high salinities during winter in some portions of the Arctic Ocean.

properties.name: IMERG/IMERG006
properties.title: Record not homogeneous: jumps at orbit and sensor changes
properties.message: IMERG is designed to give the best estimate for each grid box and time, not climate-scale consistency, so trends and interannual variability can contain artifacts from the changing satellite constellation. CORRA and GPROF, which IMERG uses for most estimates and for calibration, jump at the TRMM orbit boost (August 2001), the switch from TRMM- to GPM-based estimates (June 2014) and the GPM orbit boost (November 2023). In the Final Run, gauge adjustment helps reduce these jumps over land.
properties.instruction: For trends or interannual variability, check that the time series is consistent and the features are not artifacts of the evolving constellation; Climate Data Record products such as GPCP are designed for long-term homogeneity.

For example, the CORRA tropical values are reduced around 6% over ocean and 4% over land from the pre- to the post-boost TRMM record.
